facts.statement: Dongbeititan lived in the Early Cretaceous Yixian Formation of Beipiao, Liaoning, China.
facts.quote: Dongbeititan is a genus of sauropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous Yixian Formation of Beipiao, Liaoning, China.

facts.statement: The genus name combines the Chinese region Dongbei with the Greek word titan, meaning giant.
facts.quote: The genus name refers to the region Dongbei and to Greek titan, "giant".

facts.statement: The specific name dongi honors the Chinese paleontologist Dong Zhiming.
facts.quote: The specific name honours the Chinese paleontologist Dong Zhiming.

facts.statement: Dongbeititan was a large quadrupedal herbivore like other sauropods.
facts.quote: Like other sauropods, Dongbeititan would have been a large quadrupedal herbivore.

facts.statement: Fossils were found in the Beipiao region of western Liaoning province, north-eastern China.
facts.quote: Fossils of an unknown dinosaur were found in north-eastern China, in western Liaoning province, in the region of Beipiao.

facts.statement: The fossils were located in a valley between Libalang and Er Valleys, approximately 5 km northwest of the Sihetun Fossil Museum.
facts.quote: The bones lay in a valley between Libalang and Er Valleys, about 5 km north-western from Sihetun Fossil Museum in Beipiao.

facts.statement: In 2012, an embedded tooth of the carnivorous theropod Sinocalliopteryx was found within the holotype's incomplete thoracic rib shaft.
facts.quote: In 2012, embedded tooth of Sinocalliopteryx in the incomplete thoracic rib shaft from the holotype was described.

facts.statement: Anatomical traits suggest Dongbeititan belongs to Titanosauriformes, a sauropod group within the Macronarian line.
facts.quote: Mentioned traits suggest that the specimen belongs to Titanosauriformes, a sauropod group from Macronarian line, one of 2 main lines of evolutionarily derived sauropods.

facts.statement: Dongbeititan is classified within Somphospondyli but is not part of Titanosauria, which includes forms closer to Saltasaurus than to Brachiosaurus or Euhelopus.
facts.quote: The newly described specimen belongs to Somphospondyli too, but not to Titanosauria, defined as all Titanosauriformes closer to Saltasaurus than Brachiosaurus or Euhelopus.

facts.statement: Distinguishing traits include an anteroposteriorly elongated coracoid with a square end and a long, smooth, slightly convex acetabular margin on the pubic bone.
facts.quote: As traits distinguishing it from its relatives, they point out firstly coracoid bone elongated anteroposteriorly and of square capitoventral end and secondly long, smooth, slightly convex acetabular margin of pubic bone.

facts.statement: In 2024, Paul estimated Dongbeititan's length at 15 meters and its weight at 7 tonnes.
facts.quote: In 2024, Paul estimated its length at 15 m, and its weight at 7 t.

facts.statement: Dongbeititan lived at the beginning of the Cretaceous period, between 130 and 125 million years ago during the Barremian stage in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivió a principio del período Cretácico, entre 130 a 125 millones de años durante el Barremiense, en lo que es hoy Asia.

facts.statement: The holotype consists of a partial postcranial skeleton including limb bones, shoulder and pelvic girdles, and vertebrae.
facts.quote: El holotipo está basado en un esqueleto parcial postcranial que incluye huesos de los miembros, cintura escapular y pélvica y , vértebras.

facts.statement: Scientists describing the fossil suggest it is a basal titanosauriform, less derived than Gobititan or Jiutaisaurus but more derived than Euhelopus, Fusuisaurus, and Huanghetitan.
facts.quote: Los científicos que realizaron la descripción sugieren que se trata de un titanosauriforme basal, menos derivado que Gobititan o Jiutaisaurus, pero más que Euhelopus, Fusuisaurus, y Huanghetitan.

facts.statement: Like other sauropods, Dongbeititan was likely a large quadrupedal herbivore.
facts.quote: Como otros saurópodos, Dongbeititan debió haber sido un gran cuadrúpedo herbívoro.

facts.statement: Despite its name, Dongbeititan was not exceptionally large, likely reaching lengths of about 15 meters and a weight of approximately 7 tonnes.
facts.quote: A pesar de su nombre, este saurópodo no era demasiado grande, probablemente alcanzando longitudes de unos 15 metros y un peso de aproximadamente 7 toneladas.

facts.statement: The genus name refers to the Dongbei region and the Greek word titan, meaning giant.
facts.quote: El nombre del género se refiere a la región de Dongbei y de griego titán "gigante".

facts.statement: The fossils were found in sediments of the Jehol Group in Beipiao, Liaoning, China.
facts.quote: Encontrado en sedimentos del Grupo Jehol de Beipiao, Liaoning, China.

facts.statement: In 2012, a carnivorous theropod tooth was found embedded in a loose rib from specimen LDRCv2, which likely belongs to the holotype.
facts.quote: En 2012 se informó que en una costilla suelto, se encontró que el espécimen LDRCv2, que probablemente pertenece al holotipo, un diente de un terópodo carnívoro.

facts.statement: The type species D. dongi is the first known sauropod from the Jehol Group, which is included in the well-known Yixian Formation.
facts.quote: La especie tipo, D. dongi, es el primer saurópodo conocido del Grupo Jehol, que se encuentra incluida en la bien conocida Formación Yixian.

facts.statement: Dongbeititan is classified as a member of the parent group Somphospondyli.
facts.quote: Parent group: Somphospondyli

facts.statement: The time range for Dongbeititan is from the Barremian to the Aptian, between 125.77 and 119.57 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Aptian (125.77 to 119.57 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The genus was described in 2007 based on holotype DNHM D2867, a partial postcranial skeleton containing limb, shoulder, pelvic girdle, and vertebrae bones.
rejected.quote: It is based on holotype DNHM D2867, a partial postcranial skeleton including bones from the limbs, shoulder and pelvic girdles, and vertebrae, which was described in 2007.
